lesson_title: Perimeter, Area and Material Costs: Pricing a Yard to the Last Rand
hook_text: You measured 46 metres of fence. You just wasted R630. Here's why.
clip_script: Yard: 14 metres by 9. Walk it — 14 plus 9 plus 14 plus 9 is 46 metres. So order 46 metres of fencing, right? Wrong. There's a 2 metre gate on that line, and gates come off a different shelf. Fencing is 44 metres. At R315 a metre that's R13 860 — order the full 46 and you've thrown R630 at fence that blocks your own gateway. Now the walls. Room is 3,9 by 3,2, walls 2,6 high. Walk the floor's edge — 14,2 metres — times the height, 2,6. That's 36,92 square metres of wall. Take off the door, 1,6. Take off the window, 1,4. Thirty-three point nine two to paint. But the spec says TWO coats — so you're really covering 67,84. Paint does 7 square metres a litre, so 9,69 litres. Walk in and ask for 9,69 litres of paint. They'll stare at you. You buy two 5-litre tins. R1 120. Always round UP — running short stops the job.
visual_style: A tape measure snapping around a township yard, the gate section flashing red as it leaves the count; four walls unrolling into one long rectangle; paint tins stacking while the fractional litre gets struck out.
mood: Hands-on and practical, the confidence of someone who has priced a job before.
pacing: Quick around the fence, a hard stop at the gate, steady through the wall arithmetic, punchy at the shop counter.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and price any building job to the last rand.
